peopleAlsoAsk: Does massaman curry have meat in it?
What is the best vegetarian Thai dish?

items.markdown:
Traditional massaman curry is `not vegetarian` , as it is typically made with meat like beef, chicken, or lamb, and the paste usually contains shrimp paste or fish sauce.[](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DG32ugkypB_/?hl=en) [[1]](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DG32ugkypB_/?hl=en)[[2]](https://minimalistbaker.com/easy-1-pot-massaman-curry/)

For tips on how to prepare a plant-based version using vegan paste and tofu:![Related video thumbnail](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07280251-1672-0139-0000-4d796d98605a:4)
5m[Vegan Thai Massaman Curry - Tofu Recipe 3 years ago![](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07280251-1672-0139-0000-4d796d98605a:5)
YouTube · Love Vegan ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z_XVgpf7IQE&t=25) 

Hidden Animal Ingredients

- **Shrimp Paste:** Mixed directly into traditional store-bought and restaurant massaman curry pastes for deep umami flavor.
- **Fish Sauce:** Frequently used instead of salt to season the rich coconut milk broth.[](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DG32ugkypB_/?hl=en) [[1]](https://www.broadsheet.com.au/national/food-and-drink/article/recipe-porkfat-chef-narin-kulasais-wagyu-massaman-curry)[[2]](https://profusioncurry.com/thai-massaman-curry-with-vegetables/)

Making it Vegetarian

- **Swap the Protein:** Replace meat with firm tofu, tempeh, or extra potatoes and carrots.
- **Check the Paste:** Use a dedicated vegetarian or vegan massaman curry paste that swaps shrimp paste for soy sauce or salt.[](https://lovingitvegan.com/vegan-massaman-curry/) [[1]](https://lovingitvegan.com/vegan-massaman-curry/)[[2]](https://www.tiktok.com/@stockedfood/video/7540345023632575766)[[3]](https://sixhungryfeet.com/vegan-massaman-curry/)

expanded_element.title: Massaman curry - Wikipedia
expanded_element.description: This curry is most commonly made with chicken, but there are also variations on this dish using duck, beef, venison, mutton, goat. Pork is sometimes used, but is rare due to the dish's Muslim roots and the fact that pork is haram (forbidden) in Islam.
